name: json5
reason: Own JSON5 lexer and parse-state machine in lib/parse.js (no JSON.parse, eval or Function). JSON5 is a superset of JSON and the documented JSON5.parse(text) takes a string; the adapter decodes local bytes as strict UTF-8 and calls it once. Both valid JSON controls give a type-tagged tree equal to an independent Python json oracle and the pinned summaries, with pinned npm integrity and tarball SHA-256, V8 package-source coverage, and input-dependent AFL++ feedback verified. The path accepts JSON5-only syntax, so it does not reject invalid RFC 8259 input. Its download count mainly reflects JSON5 config-file use (e.g. via Babel), not strict JSON parsing.

name: jsonparse
reason: Own byte-level tokenizer and stack value builder behind Parser.write(Buffer). The README documents no API; the call pattern comes from the packaged example and tests. The adapter requires exactly one empty-stack root, no open container and a finished token. Both valid controls match exactly, with pinned npm integrity, V8 package-source coverage, and input-dependent AFL++ feedback verified.

name: JSONStream
reason: Distinct package API path, not an independent engine: JSONStream.parse([]) wraps one jsonparse 1.3.1 Parser in a through 2.3.8 stream and emits each completed root. Shares the jsonparse parser family. The README says an empty path emits nothing; the packaged test/test2.js and the code emit the root. Both valid controls match exactly, with pinned npm integrity for all three packages, V8 coverage counted separately for JSONStream and jsonparse, and stable AFL++ feedback whose second-control differences are all in jsonparse.js. Its stream API does not expose an end-of-input completeness check; own package source is covered but valid-control differential feedback arises only in the underlying jsonparse tokenizer.

name: @humanwhocodes/momoa
reason: Own character-level tokenizer and recursive-descent AST parser in dist/momoa.js (no JSON.parse or eval). Documented parse(text) takes a string; the adapter decodes local bytes as strict UTF-8 and calls parse(text, {mode: 'json'}), which rejects any token after the first value. Both valid controls match exactly against the AST-node summary, with pinned npm integrity and tarball SHA-256, V8 package-source coverage, and input-dependent AFL++ feedback verified.

name: lossless-json
reason: Pinned 4.3.3 parse(text) reads strictly decoded local bytes through its own recursive-descent parser. Both valid controls match an independent JSON oracle including exact LosslessNumber numeric lexemes. Docker covers 252 own parse.js lines; three-run AFL++ parser-source feedback is stable and changes by 8 features and 8 tuples. Scoped project evidence is ready for selection review.
